response.markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize **recency-balanced terminal-mask training** within the corrected BERT4Rec baseline, testing the curriculum only after a constant-mixture control. All proposed gains remain hypotheses.

**Insights and directions.** Starting-point evidence gives three insights: (1) Industrial and Electronics have 12.25% and 11.27% negative-over-positive rates. Their negative lower-tail margins motivate better discrimination rather than collapse remedies. (2) Users report stale priorities and broadly plausible recommendations. Training should emphasize specific next choices, although histories cannot establish equipment compatibility or immediate intent. (3) Collapse scores near 0.5 imply approximately zero mean cosine similarity. Empty category breakdowns cannot support category-specific explanations.

Related work supplies three insights: (1) BERT4Rec’s paper includes terminal masking, but its released training generator does not explicitly implement terminal-only examples; neither establishes a canonical frequency [1]. (2) Recency Sampling motivates recent-target emphasis, but removes sampled targets rather than constructing terminal prefixes, and evaluates other backbones [2]. (3) Adaptive hardness addresses difficult competitors, but its collaborative-filtering evidence does not establish masked-sequence benefits [3]. Replicability evidence also warns that apparent objective gains can reflect convergence differences [5].

These observations organize three directions: inference-aligned supervision, discriminative sampling, and richer item representations.

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Supervision | BERT4Rec terminal masking | Recent-prefix mixture, then curriculum | Immediate intent is unobserved |
| Sampling | Adaptive hardness | Warmed-up semi-hard negatives | False negatives and sampling bias |
| Representation | Joint history/content alignment | Scratch-trained title encoder | Sparse titles; no pretrained weights |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/future potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder.

1. **Terminal-prefix curriculum: 3/6/6/7/4.** Originality: focused adaptation (+), established terminal masking (−). Potential: inexpensive conceptual change (+), convergence and weighting may explain gains (−). User: targets stale priorities and broad-versus-specific next-choice errors (+), compatibility and current mood remain unobserved (−). Model: targets weak inference-position separation (+), diagnostic margins do not establish validation HR (−). Difficulty: unchanged architecture (+), two-view computation, budget matching and masking audits add work (−).
2. **Conservative semi-hard sampling: 4/7/5/8/4.** Originality: sequential adaptation (+), familiar mining (−). Potential: informative competitors (+), sampling bias (−). User: distinguishes close alternatives (+), intent remains implicit (−). Model: targets negative lower-tail margins (+), false negatives (−). Difficulty: unchanged architecture (+), exclusions and mining cost (−).
3. **Joint scratch title encoder: 4/6/7/5/6.** Originality: task-specific integration (+), established content features (−). Potential: finer identity cues (+), sparse text (−). User: specific artist/function clues (+), compatibility remains uncertain (−). Model: potentially sharper representations (+), collapse is absent (−). Difficulty: one joint network (+), predictor/schema changes (−). CALRec supplies conceptual context but uses prohibited pretrained weights [4].

**Selected algorithm.** Mix reconstruction with terminal prediction on training-only prefixes. Test a constant terminal weight of 0.5 before a linear 0.25→0.75 schedule. Sample terminal cutoffs equally from all eligible positions and their final quartile. This explicitly targets stale-interest ranking and broad matches outranking specific next choices, while testing weak terminal discrimination; neither user benefit is established.

```python
t = sample_training_cutoff(history, recent_mix=0.5)
x = left_pad(history[max(0, t-L+1):t] + [MASK], L)
L_terminal = CE(score_real_items(model(x)[-1]), history[t])
loss = (1-w)*mean(L_reconstruction) + w*mean(L_terminal)
```

Use identical full-catalog cross-entropy for comparisons; gather supervised states before projection [6]. Normalize objectives separately. Two views increase encoder cost, and logits scale with supervised states × catalog size; measure runtime within the shared budget. Do not introduce sampled softmax concurrently [7].

Prespecify four configurations: supplied baseline; uniform-prefix constant mixture; recent-prefix constant mixture; recent-prefix curriculum. Retain optimizer, updates and checkpoint protocol, and match supervised-target budgets in objective comparisons. The constant and scheduled mixtures have equal cumulative coefficients, but this does not guarantee equal gradient influence. Log every attempt; stop after these configurations or budget exhaustion. Do not truncate the baseline to accommodate an expensive variant.

Keep one checkpoint/category, fixed seeds, ≤200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch. Preserve routing, diagnostics and appended-mask prediction. Select solely by pinned macro **sampled** validation HR@10. If host per-user hits are available, report category-stratified paired-bootstrap differences and exploratory 95% intervals; these condition on fitted models and fixed candidates, exclude training variability, and do not correct adaptive selection bias [8–10]. Identical reevaluation adds no evidence. Recent-prefix sampling may overfit recent popularity or repeated identities; track these training-history strata without adding score components or altering evaluation.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690 and https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data.py; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643; [3] https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/28709; [4] https://research.google/pubs/calrec-contrastive-alignment-of-generative-llms-for-sequential-recommendation/; [5] https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.07483; [6] https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/master/run.py; [7] https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.07602; [8] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/; [9] https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html; [10] https://jmlr.csail.mit.edu/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html.

idea.description: Recency-balanced terminal-mask training for the supplied BERT4Rec: jointly optimize ordinary masked reconstruction and next-item prediction from strictly truncated training prefixes. Establish a constant-mixture control before testing increased terminal weighting during training.
idea.motivation: The user diagnosis identifies stale-interest recommendations and broad matches outranking specific next choices. Terminal supervision directly trains prediction of the next observed interaction from available context; recency-balanced endpoints emphasize more recent behavior. These mechanisms address both reported failures as hypotheses, without claiming to infer compatibility, mood or immediate need. Industrial_and_Scientific and Electronics have negative tenth-percentile margins, motivating a test of improved discrimination. Embedding-collapse remedies are unsupported by the measured near-zero mean cosine similarities.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain the supplied bidirectional Transformer, reserved mask token, model dimensions, optimizer, learning-rate policy, batch size and baseline reconstruction corruption policy. The proposal is relative to the supplied baseline; its exact configuration must be recorded with every run. For a history of length n >= 2, eligible zero-based target indices are E={1,...,n-1}. Define R as the final ceil(|E|/4) indices of E. Draw a Bernoulli(0.5) branch, then sample uniformly from E or R; overlap is intentional. The uniform control samples only from E. Use only training interactions, including when identifying recent endpoints. Target index t produces history[max(0,t-(L-1)):t]+[MASK], left-padded to L. The designated target event and all later events are absent; earlier occurrences of the same item ID remain legitimate context. Histories with fewer than two events are ineligible for this terminal objective.

Keep reconstruction labels separate from corrupted inputs and supervise only positions whose target identities are hidden. Use full-catalog softmax over real item IDs, excluding padding and MASK from candidate outputs, consistently in baseline and variants. Gather supervised states before vocabulary projection. Average each objective over its own valid targets before mixing. Do not introduce sampled softmax or hard-negative mining in this experiment. If the supplied baseline uses a different denominator, an explicitly labeled full-softmax baseline control is required before attributing effects to masking; account for its cost within the same budget.

For T configured optimizer updates, the constant control uses w=0.5. The curriculum uses w_s=0.25+0.5*s/(T-1), s=0,...,T-1; use 0.5 if T=1. These schedules have the same average coefficient, not necessarily equal gradient contribution. Log terminal examples, reconstruction targets, optimizer updates, wall time and GPU time. Match total supervised targets and updates across objective comparisons through a fixed target quota chosen from the supplied baseline before validation; subsample valid reconstruction targets uniformly when needed. Do not claim compute matching unless encoder tokens and runtime also match: two sequence views add computation. Record the quota and any microbatching explicitly. Memory-saving chunked projection must preserve the exact cross-entropy objective.

Prespecify the supplied baseline, uniform-prefix constant mixture, recent-prefix constant mixture and recent-prefix curriculum, with no subsequent expansion based on validation noise. Preserve the host checkpoint-selection protocol and record its evaluation cadence; if budget prevents completion, report the incomplete trial rather than silently changing its training horizon. Consider semi-hard sampling or scratch title features only as separately controlled future experiments. Recent-prefix sampling can overweight recent popular items and repeated identities. Use training-history repeat status, target frequency and prefix-length strata as secondary diagnostics; never turn them into independently fitted inference scores.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, all four categories, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution and trial-local artifacts. Each category loads exactly one independently trained selected checkpoint. No ensembles, checkpoint averaging or independent score fusion. Keep predictor writer and training architecture synchronized; inference appends MASK after retaining at most L-1 history items. With fixed-width left padding, its readout is position L-1, never nonpadding_count-1.

Preserve ModelView interfaces, including log2feats(sequence), item_emb and predict_score(features, items), plus DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader contract remains (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B×L. Diagnostic margins must use valid masked target positions and retain original IDs only as labels; terminal examples have a positive label only at MASK. Exclude padding, MASK, the target ID and observed training positives from diagnostic negative draws. Record diagnostic sampling settings and distinguish altered probes from historical measurements. Keep view.model as the actual trained nn.Module. Do not use unavailable metadata categories, ratings or review text, or interpret unidentified-item skips as negative labels.

Select using the pinned four-category macro sampled validation HR@10. If the host supplies per-user hit indicators, use 10,000 category-stratified paired bootstrap replicates with analysis seed 42, sampling 200 users with replacement within each category and using identical sampled indices for both models. Average the four category differences equally and report percentile 2.5%/97.5% bounds alongside category differences. This is exploratory uncertainty conditional on fixed models and candidate sets; it excludes training and candidate-sampling variability and is not selection-adjusted. If per-user hits are unavailable, omit the interval. Do not alter the evaluator, inspect hidden test data or claim validation gains before measurement.
idea.pseudocode:
prespecify configurations and retain supplied baseline settings
for configuration in budget_feasible_prespecified_configurations:
    for category in four_categories:
        initialize supplied BERT4Rec with seed 42
        for step in range(configured_epochs_at_most_200 * 200):
            histories = sample_training_histories_using_baseline_policy()
            reconstruction_input, labels = baseline_masked_batch(histories)
            positions = uniformly_select_hidden_targets_to_prespecified_quota(labels)
            reconstruction_states = gather(model.log2feats(reconstruction_input), positions)
            L_reconstruction = mean_full_catalog_CE(reconstruction_states, labels[positions])
            terminal_inputs, terminal_labels = [], []
            for history in eligible_histories_from_batch(histories):
                E = indices_from_1_through_len_history_minus_1(history)
                R = final_ceil_quarter(E)
                t = uniform(E) if uniform_control else uniform(choose_equal_probability(E, R))
                context = history[max(0, t-(L-1)):t]
                terminal_inputs.append(left_pad(context + [MASK], L))
                terminal_labels.append(history[t])
            terminal_states = model.log2feats(terminal_inputs)[:, -1]
            L_terminal = mean_full_catalog_CE(terminal_states, terminal_labels)
            w = 0.5 if constant_control else 0.25 + 0.5*step/max(1, total_steps-1)
            optimize((1-w)*L_reconstruction + w*L_terminal)
            log_target_counts_and_compute()
        apply_unchanged_host_checkpoint_protocol(category)
    evaluate_with_unchanged_pinned_host_evaluator()
select_one_configuration_by_macro_sampled_validation_HR_at_10()
retain_exactly_one_selected_checkpoint_per_category()
write_predictor_with_identical_architecture_and_appended_mask_inference()
report_all_attempts_and_exploratory_paired_differences_if_available()

originality.positive: Combines recency-balanced prefix selection with explicit allocation of terminal and reconstruction supervision under a tightly controlled benchmark.
originality.negative: Terminal masking appears in the original BERT4Rec paper; neither recency weighting nor curriculum learning is new. The contribution is a training-policy experiment.

future_potential.positive: Controlled comparisons can establish whether inference-aligned supervision and endpoint recency deserve further study across categories.
future_potential.negative: Observed benefits may reflect convergence, target allocation or recent popularity rather than improved intent modeling; immediate preferences and compatibility remain unobserved.

code_difficulty.positive: Preserves the backbone and candidate-scoring architecture, with changes concentrated in example construction and loss allocation.
code_difficulty.negative: Two-view training, exact full-softmax memory management, target-budget matching and family-specific diagnostic audits make reliable implementation more involved than the original rating implied.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item training with full-catalog cross-entropy.
The paper describes terminal-mask training examples to align with appended-mask inference.
limitations: Does not establish the proposed curriculum weights or recency mixture.
The released training generator does not explicitly add terminal-only examples; the paper and implementation should not be treated as specifying a canonical terminal frequency.
Terminal masking does not identify equipment compatibility or current mood.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec author implementation: training-example generation
contributions: Documents sliding windows and duplicated random-mask training samples.
Distinguishes released training generation from forced terminal masking during evaluation.
limitations: Does not establish an optimal terminal-training frequency or curriculum.
Implementation behavior should not be conflated with every mechanism described in the paper.

related_work.title: Recency-based Sampling of Sequences
contributions: Samples targets with recency-dependent probabilities and removes sampled targets from the input.
Motivates testing whether recent supervision improves sequential recommendation.
limitations: Evaluates other backbones, including GRU4Rec, Caser and SASRec.
Its multiple-target removal differs from terminal-prefix sampling; BERT4Rec transfer is unverified.

related_work.title: Adaptive Hardness Negative Sampling for Collaborative Filtering
contributions: Adapts negative hardness to address limitations of fixed sampling difficulty.
limitations: Evidence concerns collaborative filtering rather than masked BERT4Rec.
Hard-negative selection can introduce false negatives and complicate sampling corrections.
Changing sampling alongside masking would confound the initial experiment.

related_work.title: CALRec: Contrastive Alignment of Generative LLMs for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides related evidence for aligning histories and item-description representations.
limitations: Uses pretrained PaLM-2 and cannot be directly adopted under this task's constraints.
Does not validate a lightweight title encoder trained from scratch.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec replicability study
contributions: Shows that convergence and implementation efficiency can materially affect BERT4Rec comparisons.
limitations: Reported training-duration and speedup figures concern specific datasets and implementations.
Does not establish expected runtime or convergence under the fixed RecHarness budget.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec author implementation: masked-position projection and loss
contributions: Gathers prediction positions before vocabulary projection.
Normalizes masked-language-model loss using valid target weights.
limitations: Does not eliminate full-catalog projection costs.
Does not specify the proposed two-objective allocation.

related_work.title: Recommendation loss-comparison study
contributions: Provides evidence that loss choice materially affects recommendation quality.
limitations: Does not validate this terminal-mask curriculum.
Supports controlling the loss denominator rather than assuming sampled and full softmax are interchangeable.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled evaluation can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog metrics.
limitations: Does not justify modifying the pinned benchmark.
Sampled HR@10 must be interpreted within its fixed candidate protocol.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents shared-index resampling for paired observations.
limitations: Category stratification and macro aggregation must be implemented explicitly.
User bootstrap intervals exclude training variability and do not correct adaptive model selection.

related_work.title: On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how optimizing finite-sample selection criteria can cause selection bias.
limitations: Does not supply selection-adjusted intervals for this experiment.
Compact prespecified searches reduce opportunities for overfitting but do not eliminate selection bias.
